stem: A distributor needs a new company with standard setup data but no demonstration customers or transactions. Which creation option best meets that requirement?

options.text: Copy the demonstration company without reviewing its contents
Create New – No Data
Evaluation – Sample Data
Production – Setup Data Only

rationale: Use the production setup template, then import the company’s own master data. The required starting point contains setup without the sample business records.

distractors.a: An unreviewed copy can retain demonstration data.
distractors.b: No Data omits the setup that the requirement explicitly requests.
distractors.c: Evaluation includes sample business data.
distractors.d: This provides setup without demonstration business records.

stem: A consultant wants to group setup tables into Finance and Trade before building reusable configuration packages. Which feature organizes the tables into areas and groups?

options.text: Report Layout Selection
Configuration worksheet
A recurring general journal template
A saved customer list view

rationale: The configuration worksheet organizes implementation tables. Selected worksheet lines can then form a configuration package.

distractors.a: Layout selection controls report presentation.
distractors.b: Areas, groups and tables provide the required implementation hierarchy.
distractors.c: A journal template structures transactions rather than configuration-table work.
distractors.d: A saved view selects records rather than organizing implementation tables.

objective: Create and use a configuration package
stem: A prepared configuration package has been exported to Excel. Put the following remaining migration steps in a safe dependency order. Assume the package includes the needed fields and relationships.

options.text: Correct the workbook values without changing its structure.
Apply the validated package data to create or update records.
Import the edited workbook into the package.
Validate the imported package data and resolve its errors.

rationale: Edit the exported workbook, import it, validate and resolve errors, then apply. An Excel import into a package is not the same as applying the package to business tables.

distractors.a: Start by preparing the data in the workbook.
distractors.b: Applying is the last step after validation.
distractors.c: Import follows workbook preparation.
distractors.d: Validation precedes applying the package.

stem: A finance team has approved opening receivables of 80,000 and a matching control-account balance. It proposes importing rows directly into Customer Ledger Entry through a configuration package. What should the consultant recommend?

options.text: Import posted customer entries directly and separately post the same total to the G/L.
Import only the customer Balance field.
Load opening balances through a suitable journal and reconcile the resulting ledgers.
Post the entire amount only to the receivables G/L account without customer entries.

rationale: Posted ledger tables are not migration targets for configuration packages. Use supported posting routines for opening transactions so subledger and G/L evidence can be reconciled.

distractors.a: Separate direct imports still bypass the supported subledger posting process.
distractors.b: A balance field does not create an auditable opening transaction.
distractors.c: Journal posting creates supported ledger entries that can be reconciled.
distractors.d: A G/L-only balance would leave customer open entries missing.

objective: Migrate data to and within Business Central
stem: Customer migration fails validation because the imported Customer Posting Group codes do not exist in the target company. Which action addresses the cause?

options.text: Disable all validation so that nonexistent group codes are accepted.
Replace every missing code with a random existing posting group.
Map Customer Posting Group values into the Customer Price Group field instead.
Create or migrate the required posting groups, then validate the customer package again.

rationale: Referenced setup must exist before dependent records can validate. Correct the missing prerequisite rather than suppressing the validation error.

distractors.a: Suppressing validation leaves unresolved setup dependencies.
distractors.b: A code that exists can still create the wrong financial mapping.
distractors.c: Price groups control pricing and cannot replace a posting-group reference.
distractors.d: Referenced posting groups must exist before dependent customers validate.

stem: A new employee has been created in Microsoft 365 and assigned an appropriate Business Central online license. The employee is not yet listed on the Business Central Users page. What should an administrator do next?

options.text: Create a Profile (Role) with the employee’s email as its ID.
Assign a permission set to the employee’s nonexistent Business Central user record without updating user information.
Use the action to update users from Microsoft 365, then assign appropriate Business Central access.
Create a customer contact and assign it a salesperson code.

rationale: Synchronize user information from Microsoft 365 into Business Central, then configure the employee’s required permissions. A license and application authorization are separate considerations.

distractors.a: Profiles define workspaces and do not synchronize identities.
distractors.b: The application user must exist before its assignments can be managed.
distractors.c: Updating users brings the licensed identity into the application.
distractors.d: A customer contact is not an application user identity.

stem: A purchaser is assigned the Purchasing Agent profile but still cannot post a purchase invoice. What is the best explanation?

options.text: Profiles always grant SUPER.
Changing the Role Center automatically overrides all security filters.
The profile sets the workspace; effective permissions and license entitlements still control posting access.
Only the company name controls posting permissions.

rationale: Profiles shape navigation and page experience. Permission sets authorize application operations. Check the user’s effective permissions rather than treating a Role Center as a security grant.

distractors.a: A profile does not grant SUPER.
distractors.b: A Role Center cannot remove data security.
distractors.c: Workspace and authorization are distinct.
distractors.d: Company names are not authorization rules.

objective: Assign user permissions by using security groups and permission sets
stem: The sales team uses a Microsoft Entra security group. Members need the same sales permission set, restricted to company EAST. Which TWO actions are appropriate? Select two.

options.text: Assign the Sales Order Processor profile instead of the required permission set.
Link the Entra group on the Business Central Security Groups page.
Leave Company blank to restrict the assignment to EAST.
Assign the sales permission set to that group with Company set to EAST.

rationale: Link the identity group and assign company-scoped permission sets. A blank company scope would apply the assignment across companies.

distractors.a: A profile shapes the workspace and is not a substitute for authorization.
distractors.b: The group link connects membership with application permissions.
distractors.c: Blank company scope applies across companies.
distractors.d: An explicit company scope limits this permission assignment.

stem: A collections clerk may read only customers with Salesperson Code NORTH. The restriction must remain effective when the clerk removes normal page filters. Which control meets the requirement?

options.text: A normal page filter automatically inserted when the clerk opens the list
A personalized hidden Salesperson Code field
A security filter on the relevant table-data permissions
A saved list view named NORTH

rationale: Use record-level security rather than a display filter. Review all effective permission assignments so a broader access path does not defeat the intended restriction.

distractors.a: A viewing filter can be removed and is not a security boundary.
distractors.b: Hiding a field does not enforce record security.
distractors.c: A table-data security filter restricts authorized records.
distractors.d: A normal saved view can be changed by the user.

stem: A user still modifies customer records after an administrator removes Modify from one assigned permission set. Another assigned set still grants that permission. What should the administrator investigate first?

options.text: Only the removed permission-set line, without checking other assignments
The union of the user’s effective permission assignments
Only the user’s selected Profile (Role)
The customer’s credit-limit setting

rationale: Check effective permissions across assignments. Removing a grant from one set does not remove the same grant supplied by another set.

distractors.a: Another assigned set can still supply the permission.
distractors.b: Effective permissions expose the remaining authorization path.
distractors.c: The selected workspace does not explain all authorization grants.
distractors.d: Credit limits do not determine who may modify customer records.

source.title: Assign permissions to users and groups

stem: During an investigation, an administrator needs evidence of a change to a user’s permission assignment. Which built-in evidence should be examined first?

options.text: Approval entries for purchase orders
Security-related change log entries for access-control and permission tables
Only the G/L register generated by financial journals
Only the Job Queue Log Entries for scheduled reports

rationale: Business Central records changes to designated security system tables. Filter the relevant change-log evidence by user, table and time.

distractors.a: Purchase approvals do not record all permission administration changes.
distractors.b: Security table changes provide relevant audit evidence.
distractors.c: Financial registers are not an audit of user permission changes.
distractors.d: Job logs explain background-job execution rather than permission assignments.

objective: Set up and use job queues
stem: An overnight report job shows Error after a bank service outage. Which TWO actions provide a reasonable recovery and reduce repeated manual restarts? Select two.

options.text: Configure suitable maximum attempts and rerun delay for transient failures.
Delete its logs and repeatedly restart it without checking the failed dependency.
Inspect the error and restart the entry when the dependency is available.
Change the recurrence schedule while leaving the entry in Error status.

rationale: Diagnose the failure, restore the dependency and restart the job. Bounded attempts and delay can handle transient outages without treating every failure as permanent.

distractors.a: Bounded retries can handle a transient external-service outage.
distractors.b: Removing evidence and blindly retrying does not diagnose the failure.
distractors.c: Recovery should address the dependency and job state.
distractors.d: A recurrence schedule alone does not reset a failed job to a runnable state.

objective: Set up reports and configure report layouts
stem: Company EAST needs a different default invoice appearance from company WEST while keeping the same report dataset. What should the consultant configure?

options.text: Assign a document layout only to one customer while assuming it changes every customer.
Change the report ID selected for sales invoices but leave its layout unchanged.
Select the default layout for the report in the relevant company.
Change only the report’s request-page layout choice for one run.

rationale: Report layout selection is company-specific. The layout controls presentation of the report’s available data.

distractors.a: One customer-specific assignment does not establish the requested company default.
distractors.b: Changing the report object is unnecessary when its existing dataset is suitable.
distractors.c: Company-specific default layout selection meets the presentation need.
distractors.d: A temporary run-time choice does not set the company default.

source.title: Set the layout used by a report

stem: A customer card must normally receive an automatic number, but approved legacy numbers must also be enterable manually. Which number-series configuration supports both requirements?

options.text: Use a related number series but disable manual numbering on all available series.
Enable Default Nos. and Manual Nos. on the assigned series.
Enable Default Nos. but disable Manual Nos. on the series.
Enable Manual Nos. only and remove automatic default numbering.

rationale: Default numbering and permitted manual numbering are separate series settings. Enable both when both behaviors are required.

distractors.a: An alternative automatic series does not itself permit manual numbers.
distractors.b: Both automatic assignment and approved manual entry are supported.
distractors.c: That prevents the required legacy-number entry.
distractors.d: That does not meet the automatic default requirement.

stem: An available Copilot capability is inactive for the organization. Some features in this environment also require approved cross-geography processing. Which TWO configuration checks should the administrator make? Select two.

options.text: Review feature activation on Copilot & agent capabilities.
Review applicable data-movement governance and required user permissions.
Assume the selected Role Center authorizes every available AI capability.
Treat hiding a Copilot action through personalization as organization-wide feature deactivation.

rationale: Capability activation, applicable data-governance settings and feature permissions must align. Availability alone does not authorize every user or processing geography.

distractors.a: An inactive capability must be activated before use.
distractors.b: Governance and access requirements apply where relevant.
distractors.c: Role Centers are not blanket AI permission grants.
distractors.d: Personalization affects a workspace and is not an organization-wide capability switch.

stem: A consultant uses Copilot to suggest number series for a new company. The proposal includes prefixes that conflict with the customer’s numbering policy. What is the best next action?

options.text: Review and revise the proposed setup against business requirements before using it.
Accept the complete proposal without checking prefixes or setup assignments.
Skip previewing the proposed changes because suggestions cannot affect setup pages.
Treat Copilot’s proposed prefixes as an approved replacement for the customer’s numbering policy.

rationale: Assisted suggestions still require implementation review. Validate the proposed series and business controls before adopting the setup.

distractors.a: Reviewing the proposed setup is the appropriate implementation control.
distractors.b: Suggestions require review rather than automatic acceptance.
distractors.c: Accepted proposals can update number series and related setup assignments.
distractors.d: A suggestion does not supersede the approved business policy.

objective: Set up global dimensions and shortcut dimensions
stem: A company wants DEPARTMENT and PROJECT to be its two global dimensions and six additional frequently entered dimensions on document lines. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Dimensions must be represented by separate G/L accounts.
Two global dimensions plus six further shortcut dimensions fit the eight shortcut-dimension positions.
It needs ten global dimensions.
Global dimensions are in addition to eight independent shortcut dimensions.

rationale: The two global dimensions occupy the first two shortcut positions. Six further shortcut positions remain available.

distractors.a: Dimensions avoid unnecessary chart-of-account duplication.
distractors.b: The requested design uses eight shortcut positions in total.
distractors.c: Business Central supports two global dimensions.
distractors.d: The first two shortcut positions are the global dimensions.

objective: Set up default dimensions for master data
stem: Every entry for a consulting expense account must carry a PROJECT value, but the value must be selected per transaction. Which default-dimension setup meets that requirement?

options.text: Value Posting = Same Code, with Dimension Value Code fixed to INTERNAL
Hide the dimension field by personalization
Value Posting = Code Mandatory, with Dimension Value Code blank
Value Posting blank and no dimension code

rationale: Code Mandatory requires a value while allowing the transaction to supply it. Leaving the default value blank avoids imposing one project on every transaction.

distractors.a: Same Code would force the specified project.
distractors.b: Hiding a field is not a posting rule.
distractors.c: A value is required without prescribing a specific project.
distractors.d: No requirement would be enforced.

objective: Set up blocking combinations of dimensions and dimension values
stem: DEPARTMENT and PROJECT can normally coexist, but DEPARTMENT = ADMIN must never be paired with PROJECT = CUSTOMER. Which configuration is most targeted?

options.text: Delete all PROJECT dimension values.
Set the dimension combination to Limited and block only the ADMIN–CUSTOMER value pairing.
Block the entire DEPARTMENT–PROJECT dimension combination.
Create a new legal company for every project.

rationale: A limited combination lets the dimensions coexist while disallowing selected value pairs. Blocking the whole pair would reject valid combinations too.

distractors.a: Deleting all values prevents valid project analysis.
distractors.b: The limited matrix supports a specific prohibited value pair.
distractors.c: That would reject every DEPARTMENT–PROJECT pairing.
distractors.d: Separate companies do not implement the requested posting validation.

stem: A customer and an item propose different values for the same dimension on sales lines. The consultant must make the preferred source consistent for the sales source code. What should be configured?

options.text: The customer’s payment terms
Default Dimension Priorities for that source code
Only the global dimension positions in General Ledger Setup
Only the Dimension Combinations blocking matrix

rationale: Default Dimension Priorities resolve competing sources. Test document entry order and header-to-line behavior when validating the resulting values.

distractors.a: Payment terms calculate dates and discounts, not dimension precedence.
distractors.b: Priorities define the preferred table source for the transaction source code.
distractors.c: Global positions improve entry and filtering but do not rank default sources.
distractors.d: Combinations prevent invalid pairings rather than rank competing sources.

stem: A new purchase approval process must follow the implementation plan: complete approval-participant setup before creating the workflow. Put these stages in order. Users already exist, and the workflow template supports the requested event.

options.text: Copy the appropriate purchase approval workflow template.
Configure the requester, approver, limits and notification preferences.
Configure the copied workflow’s event conditions and response options.
Enable the configured workflow and test a real request using separate requester and approver accounts.

rationale: The stated implementation plan begins with participant setup. Copy the supported template before configuring its rules, then enable and test the configured process. Participant setup and template creation are not universally ordered product dependencies; the first step is explicit in this scenario.

distractors.a: Copy a supported template before modifying its workflow rules.
distractors.b: This scenario explicitly requires participant and approval-right setup first.
distractors.c: Apply business rules to the copied workflow before activation.
distractors.d: Activation and end-to-end testing follow configuration.

source.title: Set up and use a purchase approval workflow

stem: An approver sees pending requests in Business Central but wants email notifications on a defined schedule. Which setup should the consultant review?

options.text: Only the requester’s purchase amount approval limit
Approval User Setup and the approver’s Notification Setup, together with working email configuration
Only the approver’s selected Role Center
Only the workflow’s event conditions, without notification delivery setup

rationale: Approval rights and notification delivery are related but separate settings. Verify the approver’s notification method and timing and that email delivery is configured.

distractors.a: An amount limit controls approval authority rather than email delivery.
distractors.b: These settings control recipients, delivery method and timing.
distractors.c: A Role Center does not define the email notification schedule.
distractors.d: A matching event does not by itself configure notification transport and schedule.

stem: Inanda wants twelve monthly accounting periods for the fiscal year beginning 1 July 2026. Which setup meets that requirement?

options.text: Create a year starting 1 January 2026 and change only the report caption to July.
Set Allow Posting From to 1 July and assume that this creates the accounting periods.
Create a year starting 1 July 2026 with 12 periods and a period length of 1M.
Create one period of length 12D beginning 1 July 2026.

rationale: The fiscal calendar needs a July start and twelve monthly periods. Posting-date permissions are separate controls.

distractors.a: Changing a caption does not change period start dates.
distractors.b: Posting limits do not create a fiscal calendar.
distractors.c: This creates the requested monthly fiscal structure.
distractors.d: 12D represents twelve days, not twelve months.

source.title: Work with accounting periods and fiscal years

caseStudy.scenario: Inanda Field Services is preparing a new Business Central company. Its fiscal year begins on 1 July. Local currency is ZAR. Standard customers receive 30-day terms with a 2% discount for payment within 10 days. A twelve-month maintenance invoice is issued in advance. The finance team needs separate statutory and tax asset depreciation, auditable customer balances, and repeatable monthly reporting. Each question provides any additional assumptions it needs.

stem: Inanda has closed its previous fiscal year, but an accountant can still post an adjustment dated in that year. The controller wants to restrict ordinary users to the current month while permitting one authorised accountant to post earlier adjustments. What should you configure?

options.text: A different customer posting group for the accountant.
The Date Locked field on Accounting Periods for every ordinary user.
A report date filter covering only the current month.
Fixed Allow Posting From/To dates in General Ledger Setup and a deliberate exception in the accountant’s User Setup.

rationale: Closing a year does not itself prohibit posting. Company posting limits and controlled user-specific exceptions address this requirement.

distractors.a: Customer posting groups select receivables accounts, not user posting rights.
distractors.b: Date Locked protects the period structure rather than user posting dates.
distractors.c: A report filter changes the view, not posting validation.
distractors.d: The company boundary and authorised user override enforce the required separation.

stem: Inanda creates an invoice with a document date of 4 August and a posting date of 8 August. The payment terms use a due-date formula of 30D and a discount-date formula of 10D, with 2% discount. Ignoring tax and rounding, which result should you expect for a ZAR 10,000 invoice?

options.text: Due immediately because payment terms require the posting and document dates to match.
Due 7 September; discount deadline 18 August; eligible discount ZAR 200.
Due 3 September; discount deadline 14 August; eligible discount ZAR 200.
Due 3 September; discount deadline 14 August; eligible discount ZAR 2,000.

rationale: Payment terms calculate these dates from the document date. Thirty days after 4 August is 3 September; ten days after is 14 August. Two percent of 10,000 is 200.

distractors.a: Different document and posting dates do not invalidate payment terms.
distractors.b: This incorrectly uses the posting date as the date-formula basis.
distractors.c: Both date calculations and the percentage match the stated terms.
distractors.d: This treats 2% as 20%.

stem: Inanda agrees that a customer will pay by bank transfer and must pay within 30 days. You need defaults for new invoices. Which configuration separates the two requirements correctly?

options.text: Set Payment Method Code to the bank-transfer method and Payment Terms Code to the 30-day terms.
Enter the customer’s bank account number in the Due Date field.
Create a customer posting group called BANK30 and rely on its name.
Set Payment Terms Code to the bank-transfer method and leave Payment Method Code blank.

rationale: The method describes the means of payment, while the terms control due dates and discounts. Their codes belong in separate master-data fields.

distractors.a: This records both independent defaults in their appropriate fields.
distractors.b: An account identifier cannot replace a due date.
distractors.c: Posting group names do not define terms or methods.
distractors.d: A payment method is not a due-date formula.

stem: Inanda invoices ZAR 120,000, excluding tax, for twelve equal monthly service periods. The accountant wants exactly ZAR 10,000 recognised in each period, without variation for the number of days in a month. Which deferral calculation method should the template use?

options.text: User-Defined, leaving all schedule amounts blank.
Equal per Period, with 12 periods and a reviewed start date.
Days per Period, because every month contains an identical number of days.
A payment term of 12M, with no deferral template.

rationale: Equal per Period divides the amount evenly across the specified periods. The recognition schedule also needs the correct start date and deferral account.

distractors.a: User-defined schedules require entered amounts; blanks do not establish the allocation.
distractors.b: This produces twelve equal allocations of the stated amount.
distractors.c: Calendar months differ in length, so this does not express the equal-amount requirement.
distractors.d: Payment terms control settlement timing rather than revenue recognition.

stem: Inanda will invoice a customer in EUR while retaining ZAR as local currency. Which TWO setup actions are appropriate? Select two.

options.text: Replace the company’s local currency with EUR for each invoice.
Create and configure EUR in Currencies, including relevant accounts and exchange rates.
Set EUR as the default Currency Code on the customer card.
Create ZAR again as a foreign currency and assign it to every local customer.

distractors.b: A foreign-currency code needs its supporting setup.
distractors.c: This provides the default transaction currency for this customer.

stem: An accountant has created account 6100 as a Heading, then tries to select it for a direct expense journal line. The account should hold individual expense entries. Which change addresses the design error?

options.text: Set Account Type to Total and include account 6100 in its Totaling filter.
Use an account whose Account Type is Posting for the expense entries.
Enable Direct Posting while retaining Account Type Heading.
Set Account Type to Begin-Total and assign the Expenses account category.

rationale: Heading and total-type accounts organise the chart. Transaction accounts must be posting accounts, with other posting controls configured appropriately.

distractors.a: A Total account aggregates other accounts; it does not receive individual expense postings.
distractors.b: A Posting account is the relevant chart structure for individual ledger entries.
distractors.c: Direct Posting does not convert a Heading into a Posting account.
distractors.d: A Begin-Total account structures an account range; its category does not make it a transaction account.

stem: A new expense G/L account is missing from category-based financial statements. Which TWO checks are most relevant before changing the report calculation? Select two.

options.text: Confirm the category-based report definitions reflect the intended category structure.
Confirm the G/L account is assigned to the intended account category/subcategory.
Recreate every posted transaction in a new company.
Change the customer’s Shipment Method Code.

rationale: Category-driven statements depend on account categorisation and the definitions built from that structure. Diagnose those mappings before introducing unrelated changes.

distractors.a: The definitions must represent the expected category layout.
distractors.b: An uncategorised or miscategorised account can be excluded from the intended report grouping.
distractors.c: Recreating transactions is unnecessary and disrupts the audit trail.
distractors.d: Shipment methods do not define financial statement groupings.

objective: Prepare financial reporting with financial data and account categories
stem: The controller wants one report with revenue, cost of sales and gross profit as rows, and current-month actual, prior-year actual and budget as columns. Which design is appropriate?

options.text: A financial report combining a row definition for the account groupings/formula and a column definition for the comparison measures.
Three customer posting groups named CURRENT, PRIOR and BUDGET.
A bank reconciliation with each revenue account as a statement line.
A number series containing the names of the requested columns.

rationale: Financial reporting separates the row calculations from the time/value comparisons in columns. This supports a repeatable statement without changing transaction posting.

distractors.a: Rows and columns each express the relevant part of the reporting requirement.
distractors.b: Customer posting groups select receivables control accounts rather than report measures.
distractors.c: Reconciliation matches bank activity, not profit measures.
distractors.d: Number series identify records and documents.

stem: An ordinary general journal must distribute a ZAR 18,000 administration cost as 60% to one destination G/L account and 40% to another. The split is stable each month. Which setup is the most direct fit?

options.text: A variable allocation based on changing statistical balances, with no source balances defined.
One customer posting group for each percentage.
Two payment terms with due-date formulas of 60D and 40D.
A fixed allocation account with the two destinations and 60/40 shares; test the distribution before posting.

rationale: A fixed allocation expresses a stable split. For this test amount the destinations receive ZAR 10,800 and ZAR 7,200 before any applicable tax handling.

distractors.a: A variable allocation needs an appropriate changing basis and is unnecessary here.
distractors.b: Customer posting groups do not distribute this expense.
distractors.c: Due-date formulas do not allocate costs.
distractors.d: The setup matches the fixed distribution and provides a preposting test.

stem: A wholesaler wants product revenue for domestic customers and export customers to post to different revenue accounts, while using the same item. Which TWO statements correctly describe the setup? Select two.

options.text: Assign appropriate General Business Posting Groups to the customer records.
Use only the item’s Inventory Posting Group to distinguish domestic and export customers.
Create a different accounting period for export sales.
Configure the relevant business/product combinations in General Posting Setup with their revenue accounts.

rationale: The business classification identifies the trading party, and the product classification identifies what is sold. Their configured combination determines the revenue account.

distractors.a: The customer business classification expresses the domestic/export distinction.
distractors.b: Inventory posting groups govern inventory valuation accounts rather than customer-based revenue selection.
distractors.c: Time periods do not encode the customer market.
distractors.d: The matrix supplies the G/L account for each relevant combination.

stem: A sales invoice posts to the correct revenue account but to the wrong receivables control account. Which setup should you inspect first?

options.text: The Sales Account in General Posting Setup for the business/product combination.
The Inventory Account in Inventory Posting Setup for the item and location.
The Invoice Rounding Account on the customer posting group.
The customer posting group used by the invoice and its Receivables Account mapping.

rationale: Revenue and receivables use different posting mappings. The customer posting group links the customer subledger to its receivables control account.

distractors.a: This mapping selects sales revenue, which the scenario says is already correct.
distractors.b: This mapping affects inventory value, not the customer receivables control account.
distractors.c: The rounding account handles invoice-rounding differences; it does not replace the Receivables Account mapping.
distractors.d: This is the mapping responsible for the receivables side of the posting.

stem: Item STOCK-A has Inventory Posting Group RESALE. Its inventory value should post to a separate balance-sheet account at location CAPE compared with location JOBURG. Which setup provides that distinction?

options.text: General Posting Setup for the general business and general product posting group combination.
Default receipt and shipment bins on the two location cards.
The Inventory Posting Group code on the item, without configuring location-specific Inventory Posting Setup.
Inventory Posting Setup for the relevant location and inventory posting group combinations.

rationale: Inventory Posting Setup links the location/inventory posting group combination to the inventory G/L accounts. It is separate from sales revenue mapping.

distractors.a: General Posting Setup controls combinations such as revenue and cost-of-sales mappings; the location-based inventory balance-sheet mapping is elsewhere.
distractors.b: Bins control physical stock handling within a location, not the inventory G/L account selection.

stem: A customer normally uses one receivables posting group but may use an approved alternative on selected documents. Which THREE configuration actions are required? Select three.

options.text: Delete the customer’s default posting group.
Replace all general product posting groups with bank account posting groups.
Enable Allow Multiple Posting Groups in Sales & Receivables Setup.
Define the permitted alternatives using Alternative Groups for the customer posting group.
Enable Allow Multiple Posting Groups on the relevant customer card.

rationale: Alternative posting groups are explicitly enabled at application setup and customer level, with allowed substitutes configured. Retain controlled defaults.

distractors.a: The default remains useful and is not deleted to enable alternatives.
distractors.b: Product and bank posting groups have unrelated roles.
distractors.c: The application setting enables the capability for customer posting groups.

stem: A consultant creates a bank account card and its linked G/L account. The accountant wants all operational bank movements to have bank ledger entries so that reconciliation remains possible. Which control best supports this design?

options.text: Set the linked G/L account type to Heading.
Set the bank account Currency Code to the customer number.
Avoid creating a bank card and post every bank transaction directly to its G/L account.
Link the card through a Bank Account Posting Group and normally disable Direct Posting on the linked G/L account.

rationale: Posting via the bank account preserves both the bank subledger and its control account. Direct G/L-only postings can cause reconciliation differences.

distractors.a: A heading cannot serve as the posting control account.
distractors.b: A customer identifier is not a currency code.
distractors.c: G/L-only movements do not create the required bank ledger entries.
distractors.d: This connects the ledgers and discourages bypassing the bank subledger.

stem: Two accountants must maintain separate unposted journal lines while sharing the same general-journal type and default structure. Which setup should you choose?

options.text: One shared batch, with a different document-number prefix for each accountant.
One shared batch, with a different Reason Code on each accountant’s lines.
One shared batch, with each accountant assigned a different default balancing account.
Two named batches under the same journal template.

rationale: Templates define the journal category and common structure. Batches provide separate working sets of journal lines within that template. This is working-set separation, not a claim that a batch alone restricts another user’s access.

distractors.a: Number prefixes identify documents but do not create separate journal working sets.
distractors.b: Reason codes describe postings; the unposted lines would still occupy one batch.
distractors.c: Balancing-account defaults do not partition the batch’s unposted lines.
distractors.d: Separate batches provide distinct working sets under the shared template. They are not a substitute for permissions if user-level security isolation is also required.

source.title: Set up general journal templates and batches

objective: Create journal templates including number series
stem: An accounts team wants a payment-journal batch to propose document numbers from a dedicated sequence when new journal lines are entered. It is not requesting a separate renumbering sequence at posting. Where should the consultant configure the entry-time default?

options.text: Use the Sales Invoice Nos. series in Sales & Receivables Setup.
Set only the batch’s Posting No. Series, leaving its No. Series blank.
Assign the dedicated series to No. Series in the payment-journal batch setup.
Assign a dedicated Source Code to the journal template.

rationale: Use the journal batch’s No. Series for the document-number proposal during entry. Posting No. Series is a separate control for numbering at posting. Sales numbering and source codes serve different purposes.

distractors.a: Sales-document numbering does not establish the payment-journal batch’s proposed document numbers.
distractors.b: Posting No. Series controls numbering at posting; it does not replace the batch’s entry-time No. Series default.
distractors.c: The batch’s No. Series provides proposed document numbers for its journal lines.
distractors.d: A source code identifies the posting origin for the audit trail; it is not a document-number sequence.

stem: A monthly recurring journal has two lines: a fixed ZAR 5,000 charge and an amount that must be entered anew each month. The accountant wants the first amount retained and the second cleared after posting. Which recurring methods fit?

options.text: Fixed for ZAR 5,000 and Variable for the changing amount.
Variable for both lines because both recur monthly.
Balance for both lines regardless of the source accounts.
Fixed for both lines and assume both amounts are cleared.

rationale: The recurring method determines how line amounts behave after posting. Fixed retains the amount; Variable clears it for the next entry.

distractors.a: The two methods match the different reuse requirements.
distractors.b: Variable would clear the fixed amount as well.
distractors.c: Balance methods use account balances and do not describe this fixed-versus-reentered requirement.
distractors.d: Fixed does not clear the amount after posting.

objective: Create vendor accounts and set up payment journals
stem: A supplier will be paid using a supported payment-file export. Which THREE records/settings should the consultant validate as part of setup? Select three.

options.text: The supplier’s recipient bank account and the relevant payment details.
Allow Payment Export on the payment-journal batch.
A sales blanket order for the supplier.
A financial-report category named EXPORT.
The company bank account’s supported payment export format.

rationale: Payment-file preparation depends on recipient data, the bank-format configuration and an enabled payment batch. The bank still requires its own submission/authorisation process.

distractors.a: The file needs valid recipient account details.
distractors.b: The batch must permit payment export.
distractors.c: A sales blanket order does not configure vendor banking.
distractors.d: A report category does not configure file export.
distractors.e: The format must match a supported requirement of the paying bank.

source.title: Set up banking and bank connections

objective: Assess the relationship between vendors and ledger entries
stem: A vendor invoice is ZAR 8,000. A payment of ZAR 3,000 has been posted and applied. The accountant needs to explain why the invoice’s remaining amount is now ZAR 5,000 without altering the original invoice. Which evidence chain is most useful?

options.text: A manually edited original invoice amount of ZAR 5,000.
Only the latest purchase quote, because quotes change remaining amounts.
Only the vendor’s name and address.
The vendor’s invoice/payment ledger entries, their detailed application entries, and the corresponding G/L control-account entries.

rationale: The original invoice remains part of the audit trail. Payment and application detail explain the remaining balance, while the G/L entries support control-account reconciliation.

distractors.a: Changing the original posted amount would destroy the explanation rather than provide it.
distractors.b: An unposted quote does not settle an invoice.
distractors.c: Master-data contact details cannot explain settlement movements.
distractors.d: These linked records explain the transaction, settlement and accounting effects.

stem: A receivables team wants a list of open sales documents where it can mark Payment Made, enter received amounts and dates, and register receipts. It will enter this information manually rather than prepare individual cash receipt journal lines. Which capability most directly provides that workspace?

options.text: Payment Registration, with the appropriate setup for registering customer payments.
A cash receipt journal with manually entered customer lines and Applies-to Doc. No.
Bank Account Reconciliation to match bank statement lines to existing bank ledger entries.
A payment journal using Suggest Vendor Payments.

rationale: Payment Registration provides a focused receivables payment-registration experience. Demonstrate it against open customer documents using the intended setup.

distractors.a: Payment Registration is the focused list-based workspace described in the requirement.
distractors.b: A cash receipt journal can post receipts, but does not provide the requested Payment Made checklist over open sales documents.
distractors.c: Bank reconciliation matches statement information against bank ledger entries; it is not the requested open-sales-document registration checklist.
distractors.d: Suggest Vendor Payments prepares supplier payments, rather than this customer-receipt workflow.

source.title: Configure financials: set up payment registration

objective: Create customer accounts and related records
stem: A newly created customer must default to 14-day settlement and EUR invoicing. Which master-data values should be set?

options.text: Payment Method Code for a bank transfer and Currency Code EUR, with no Payment Terms Code.
Payment Terms Code for the 14-day terms and Currency Code EUR on the customer.
Payment Terms Code for 14-day terms and EUR as the company’s additional reporting currency, leaving the customer Currency Code blank.
Payment Terms Code for 14-day terms and EUR exchange-rate records, leaving the customer Currency Code blank.

rationale: Customer defaults capture settlement terms and transaction currency. The company’s local currency remains company-wide.

distractors.b: These fields provide the two requested defaults.

distractors.d: Exchange rates support EUR conversion, but do not by themselves select EUR on the customer’s documents.

source.title: Set up currencies and exchange rates

stem: One machine needs a financial-reporting depreciation schedule and a different tax schedule. Only the financial-reporting book should integrate its relevant postings with the G/L. Which TWO design decisions are appropriate? Select two.

options.text: Configure the G/L Integration settings deliberately for each book.
Assume every depreciation book must always post to the G/L.
Use separate depreciation books for the two purposes and assign the required books to the asset.
Create the tax schedule by renaming the machine after every calculation.

rationale: Depreciation books let the same asset support different valuation purposes. Their integration settings determine which asset activities affect the G/L.

distractors.a: Integration is a book-level design decision and should not be assumed identical.
distractors.b: A nonintegrated book can serve another depreciation purpose.
distractors.c: Separate books support distinct accounting purposes for one asset.
distractors.d: Asset names do not define depreciation schedules.

source.title: Set up general fixed assets information

objective: Configure fixed asset classes and subclasses
stem: A company wants to classify assets first as TANGIBLE or INTANGIBLE, then separate tangible assets into VEHICLES and MACHINERY for analysis. Which setup is the closest fit?

options.text: Fixed asset classes with appropriate fixed asset subclasses.
A new user permission set for each machine.
One currency code for each asset family.
Customer shipment methods named VEHICLES and MACHINERY.

rationale: Classes and subclasses provide fixed-asset classification. They should be designed alongside depreciation and posting requirements, without confusing classification with those controls.

distractors.a: The two classification levels express the intended asset grouping.
distractors.b: Permissions govern access, not asset categories.
distractors.c: Currency codes identify monetary units.
distractors.d: Shipment methods do not classify fixed assets.

stem: A production line consists of a frame and replaceable motor that need separate fixed-asset records but should also be analysed as one main asset. What should you do?

options.text: Use only an item variant and delete all fixed-asset records.
Create one G/L Heading account and assume it automatically creates components.
Enter every component as text in one customer’s address.
Create the main asset and component assets as individual fixed assets, then assign components on the main asset’s component list.

rationale: The main-asset/component relationship groups individual fixed-asset records. It does not replace their individual setup.

distractors.a: Item variants do not create fixed-asset component relationships.
distractors.b: A chart heading does not create asset records or links.
distractors.c: A customer address has no asset-structure function.
distractors.d: This preserves separate asset records and establishes the reporting relationship.

source.title: Set up main assets and asset components

stem: An asset costs ZAR 120,000 and has an expected salvage value of ZAR 20,000 after five complete years. Assuming no later changes and equal full-year straight-line depreciation, what annual amount should the setup imply?

options.text: ZAR 100,000 every year.

rationale: The depreciable basis is 120,000 minus 20,000, or 100,000. Spreading that evenly over five full years gives 20,000 per year.

distractors.a: This ignores the salvage value.
distractors.b: This adds the salvage value to cost before dividing.
distractors.c: This allocates the depreciable basis evenly over five years.
distractors.d: This repeats the entire depreciable basis each year.

stem: A controller wants accelerated depreciation calculated using a declining balance rather than the same annual amount throughout the asset’s life. Which family of methods should you evaluate?

options.text: A financial-report column labelled DEPRECIATION.
Equal per Period deferral calculation.
Declining-Balance methods, with the chosen method’s rate and calculation rules reviewed.
A customer payment-discount percentage.

rationale: Declining-balance depreciation applies the configured rules to a reducing basis. It is an asset valuation method rather than a report label or settlement discount.

distractors.a: A report label does not configure an asset’s calculation.
distractors.b: Deferral schedules allocate document revenue or expense and are not fixed-asset depreciation methods.
distractors.c: This is the relevant depreciation method family.
distractors.d: Payment discounts affect invoice settlement.

objective: Configure fixed asset general ledger integration
stem: The DEPR book has G/L Integration enabled for depreciation. Which journal should be used for an integrated depreciation transaction?

options.text: A sales quote.
A nonintegrated Fixed Asset Journal, assuming it automatically creates identical G/L entries.
An Inventory Reclassification Journal.
Fixed Asset G/L Journal.

rationale: When an asset activity is integrated with the general ledger, its transactions use the Fixed Asset G/L Journal. A nonintegrated journal is not an interchangeable route.

distractors.a: A quote does not record depreciation.
distractors.b: The nonintegrated route does not satisfy the stated G/L integration requirement.
distractors.c: Inventory reclassification does not post asset depreciation.
distractors.d: This is the journal for the integrated fixed-asset activity.

stem: A sandbox has no receivables G/L account or customer posting group. Place the following dependency steps in order so that a test customer invoice can use the new control account.

options.text: Create a fresh test invoice for that customer and preview the posting.
Create the receivables G/L posting account.
Assign the customer posting group to the test customer.
Create a customer posting group and map its Receivables Account to that account.

rationale: The posting account must exist before it can be selected in the group, and the customer needs the group before a new invoice inherits it. Preview validates the resulting mapping.

distractors.a: Finally test the inherited setup on a new document.
distractors.b: First establish the G/L destination.
distractors.c: Next give the test customer the configured group.
distractors.d: Then map the group to the existing destination.

stem: A consultant is creating a new deferral setup from scratch. Order these dependent steps for a sandbox validation. Assume all other posting setup already exists.

options.text: Apply the template to a test document line and review its deferral schedule.
Create the deferral template and select that account and the intended calculation rules.
Preview the document posting and compare the period amounts with the requirement.
Create the required balance-sheet deferral G/L account.

rationale: The template refers to an existing account. A document line uses that template to form a schedule, and preview then checks its accounting effect before posting.

distractors.a: A test line then provides the amount and date context.
distractors.b: The template supplies the account and schedule defaults.
distractors.c: Preview is the final validation of the configured accounting effect.
distractors.d: The referenced account must exist first.

source.title: Set up and validate a deferral template

stem: A consultant is designing two distributions: a stable 70/30 overhead split and a staff-cost split driven by changing departmental headcounts. Which TWO statements are correct? Select two.

options.text: Both requirements are solved by changing payment discount dates.
A variable allocation account can use an appropriate statistical-account basis for the changing headcounts.
A fixed allocation automatically reads a changing headcount even when no basis is configured.
A fixed allocation account fits the stable 70/30 split.

rationale: The allocation type should match whether the basis is deliberately fixed or varies with a measured source. Validate destination accounts and the resulting percentages.

distractors.a: Settlement discounts do not allocate departmental costs.
distractors.b: A configured statistical basis can drive the changing distribution.
distractors.c: A fixed rule does not infer an external or changing driver.
distractors.d: The stable rule is directly expressed as a fixed distribution.

source.title: Use general ledger allocations in Business Central

stem: A foreign-currency setup has exchange rates but no realised gain/loss G/L account mappings. The consultant is asked whether the rate table alone is sufficient for production. What is the best answer?

options.text: No. Put the realised gain/loss accounts only in General Posting Setup for the foreign customer’s business/product combination.
No. Configure and validate the relevant currency posting accounts as well as exchange-rate data.
Yes. Configuring only unrealised gain/loss accounts covers both open-entry adjustments and every settlement difference.
Yes. Payment-tolerance accounts automatically replace missing currency gain/loss mappings.

rationale: A rate converts amounts, but accounting differences also need configured G/L destinations. A test transaction should validate the setup before production use.

distractors.a: General Posting Setup does not replace the currency’s realised gain/loss account configuration.
distractors.b: Rates and posting-account configuration are complementary requirements.
distractors.c: Unrealised adjustment accounts do not replace the realised accounts required for applicable settlement differences.
distractors.d: Payment tolerances handle permitted settlement differences under their own rules; they do not substitute for currency gain/loss account setup.

stem: An accountant wants to split a recurring rent journal using percentage allocation keys. They see Allocation Account in the Account Type list and assume it is supported in recurring journals. Which guidance is correct?

options.text: Replace the recurring journal with a customer statement report.
Use Allocation Account because every visible option is supported in every journal.
Change the document date until the option begins working.
Use the recurring journal’s Allocations action and allocation keys; allocation accounts are not supported in recurring journals.

rationale: Recurring-journal allocations use their own allocation keys. The visible account-type option does not make allocation accounts supported in that journal.

distractors.a: A customer statement reports balances and does not replace a recurring cost journal.
distractors.b: A visible option alone is not proof of support in that context.
distractors.c: The journal feature limitation is not a date-validation problem.
distractors.d: This uses the supported recurring-journal allocation mechanism.

stem: A dealer sells individually identified high-value machines. The cost of each serial-numbered unit must follow that exact unit through the sale. Which costing method best matches the requirement?

options.text: Average
Specific
LIFO chosen solely because the unit has a serial number
Standard

rationale: Specific costing matches the identifiable unit’s receipt cost to its outbound transaction. Item tracking and costing configuration must support that requirement.

distractors.a: Average pools costs rather than identifying one receipt cost.
distractors.b: Specific uses the received cost of the particular unit.
distractors.c: Serial identification alone does not make LIFO the required cost flow.
distractors.d: Standard uses a maintained standard with variances.

stem: A manufacturer wants inventory valued at a maintained planned unit cost and wants purchase-cost differences recorded as variances. Which method should the consultant evaluate?

options.text: Standard
FIFO
Specific
Average

rationale: Standard costing uses the maintained standard rather than adopting each receipt’s actual cost as inventory value. Variance handling is part of the design.

distractors.a: A maintained standard and variances match the requirement.
distractors.b: FIFO follows receipt cost flow.
distractors.c: Specific follows the exact unit’s cost.
distractors.d: Average calculates pooled actual cost.

stem: The same item needs different reorder points and vendors at the EAST and WEST locations. Both locations must retain the same item number. Which setup is appropriate?

options.text: An item variant used only as a substitute for location-specific replenishment data
A single item card reorder point applied unchanged to both locations
Vendor item references for each location, using the references instead of location-specific replenishment parameters.
Stockkeeping units for the item-location combinations

rationale: Stockkeeping units supplement the item with location- and optionally variant-specific planning data. They avoid duplicating the item solely for replenishment differences.

distractors.a: A variant alone does not supply the required location-specific planning identity.
distractors.b: One shared parameter cannot represent different location policies.
distractors.c: Vendor item references identify an item for a trading partner; they do not establish the location-specific reorder point and replenishment policy.
distractors.d: SKUs provide location-specific replenishment settings.

options.text: 60 PCS
12 PCS
17 PCS
5 PCS

distractors.a: Five boxes contain sixty base pieces.
distractors.b: That is one box only.
distractors.c: Adding quantities is not the conversion rule.
distractors.d: That ignores the box conversion.

stem: A retailer must retain one item number for a chair model sold in RED and BLUE. It wants inventory availability by color and a searchable material characteristic such as WOOD. Which TWO setups fit? Select two.

options.text: Use a Color item attribute to create separate reservable stock balances for RED and BLUE.
Use RED and BLUE as item units of measure, both equal to 1 PCS, to distinguish color availability.
Use an item attribute for material.
Use item variants for RED and BLUE.

distractors.a: An attribute describes the item; it does not create separate variant-level quantity or reservation identities.
distractors.b: Units of measure express quantity conversions. They are not an alternative stock identity for color variants.
distractors.c: Material is a descriptive item characteristic.
distractors.d: Variants support availability by the item’s color version.

Use a different bill-to customer for every delivery site solely to select the delivery address.
Set up ship-to addresses for the customer.
Use customer bank account codes as delivery-address identifiers.

Vendor order addresses
A remit-to address used as the sole control for ordering and delivery timing
Payment Terms Code used to calculate the stock’s planned receipt date

The minimum quantity condition is not met.

rationale: After the line discount, 10,000 × 0.90 = 9,000. The invoice discount is 9,000 × 0.05 = 450. The final amount is 8,550.

distractors.b: This ignores the line discount.

stem: A vendor offers a document-total discount once eligible purchases exceed 20,000. The consultant must configure a percentage based on the qualifying invoice total rather than an item quantity. Which setup is appropriate?

An item-specific purchase line discount with a minimum quantity only
The customer payment discount tolerance
A warehouse bin ranking

rationale: Vendor invoice discounts apply to an eligible document total. Item-level line discounts solve a different pricing requirement.

distractors.a: Invoice discount terms provide the amount threshold and percentage.
distractors.b: Quantity-based line discounts do not implement this document-total threshold.
distractors.c: Customer payment tolerance concerns incoming payments.

stem: A consultant must explain why a later item-charge invoice can change inventory value without adding more units. Which explanation is correct?

Item ledger entries record quantity movements; value entries record cost amounts associated with those movements.
Every value entry must add at least one unit of inventory.

Only assigning a default Location Code to a customer
Location Mandatory in Inventory Setup

objective: Differentiate designing, customizing, and personalizing pages
stem: A purchasing clerk wants to move a field and hide an unused column for their own workspace. Other users must retain their current layout. Which approach meets this requirement?

Save the filtered list as a named view.

stem: A customer disputes invoice INV-410. The consultant needs the customer ledger, general ledger, and item entries generated by that posted document. What is the most direct investigation?

distractors.b: A summary customer balance does not identify all ledger and item entries from this invoice.
distractors.c: Correct: it follows the posted document’s related records.
distractors.d: Changing master data does not explain the original posted entries.

stem: Support must identify the table behind a custom list and which installed extension changes that page. Which TWO statements are accurate?
